ProjectPullRequestView.review: 'critic' | 'you' | 'none' | null (null for Forerunner's docs PRs). Any screen that lists a task's PR or calls it 'reviewed' should read this field, not the task's reason: at level 2 the merge writes 'PR left open for you: ...' over the critic's words.

session/findings.ts exports ACCEPTED_AT_SIGNOFF ('you accepted the work at sign-off'), used where findings.ts wrote that literal. verification: if the sign-off or Mark-done reasons change, reviewOf in daemon/pull-requests.ts reads them with startsWith, together with ACCEPTED_WITHOUT_REVIEW from @forerunner/critic.
session/result.ts: the PR sentence is now 'Left N reviewed pull request(s) for you to merge.' (what the session did), no longer '... wait for you to merge.'

capabilities githost: push-words.ts exports pushFailure(e), pushFailedWords(repo, branch, e) and firstPushFailedWords(repo, e). ensureBaseBranch throws firstPushFailedWords text with code provider_auth for a refusal (not transient for the runner) and provider_error otherwise; details.failure is the kind.
agent/sdk.ts: scrubGitConfigEnv drops any git config entry whose key or value holds a URL with a user part (ssh://git@ included), an Authorization header or a token shape.

The Files tab text "This computer's copy of <repo> as merged" is stale between a merge on GitHub and the next session: after merging #1 on the host, notes.html was missing until a session refreshed the docs clone (step 50). Fetch and reset the clone when Files is opened, or say "as of the last session".

The "GitHub did not answer" text on the Overview embeds the error text in parentheses (pull-requests.ts:75). A project whose GitHub token is missing would also read "GitHub did not answer", which is not true then. Design §5.8.

Every session on a repository project leaves a status PR for the person to merge (even a one-task project). This follows ADR 0104 and is defensible; the owner may want the status kept off GitHub until asked.

A repository project's status sentence is just "Done: all N tasks." with no pointer to where the work is. Design §2 rule 6 has "Your files: <path>"; for a repository, "Your files: on GitHub, 6 pull requests to merge" would keep that.
The branch shown on the session page ("branch fr/01a19c00-create-...") carries an 8-character task-id prefix (pre-existing branch naming; design §5.3 says no ids).

Pre-existing, not this area: the folder project's "Code work is planned for Folder page, which has no repository ... with no branch, pull request or review on GitHub. Create a repository for it?" card makes a finished project read "Waiting for you: 1 question" on Home. Design §3.8 does not list this card type, and "no ... review" is not true (the critic reviews folder tasks).

The brief promises that git's read commands work in the folder. That holds in the process sandbox; whether the Docker runner image (forerunner-runner) has git installed was not checked here, since the image is built elsewhere.

Sibling not covered: packages/runtime/src/data/import.ts:601 creates the migration branch from origin/<default> without ensureBaseBranch, so a data import into an empty repository would still fail with git's text. This is outside this area's journeys.

The fixer's new_problems stand and are confirmed on the bench: all task branches start from main, so a dependent task does not see its dependency's unmerged work (five sibling branches in every graph). This needs an owner decision (stacked PRs or merging dependency branches).
The real-daemon case for waiting PRs inserts the done task directly into the store rather than running a session; the bench walk covers the session path.

{"problem": "Research on a Claude subscription (the SDK path): the Agent SDK's WebFetch is still checked against the run token's domain list, which is empty for the researcher, so every page is refused there; WebSearch works.", "why": "The owner's decision named the API-key path. {"problem": "Ports are not restricted for public hosts, and machines behind a mandatory proxy cannot read pages", "why": "Kept simple. The client connects directly and ignores proxy variables. Both are recorded in ADR 0107 as known gaps."}

Subscription path: research reads no page. packages/runtime/src/agent/cc-tools.ts gives WebFetch domainFields ['url'], and the executor derives the run token's allowedDomains from the registry's allowed_domains, which is [] for the researcher. On a subscription the hooks therefore deny every WebFetch outside github.com (security-sdk.test.ts asserts domain denial); WebSearch works. Tasks use the subscription first by default (user guide).

No API view carries a project's version, and no screen edits settings.browser (the site list and block list web_fetch and the browser read). PUT /projects/:id/settings needs the version, which a client can only learn from the 409 conflict answer (seen on the bench walk).

Still present, owned by continuity: other executor refusals (task budget spent, unknown specialist, retry ladder with no stand-in) still end as needs_human with no Inbox card. Only the missing-web-tool case is gone.

Plan card: a plan task naming a specialist this install does not have (an invented name) is not flagged. The intake canonicalises aliases only when it writes the plan, so the UI cannot tell an alias from an unknown name; the run then waits with 'No specialist is named X'.

The ADR and the fixer's new_problems both say that path refuses every WebFetch, because the researcher's allowed_domains is empty, so research there reads no page and only search works. The task drawer does not show which web pages a run read or which were refused. The plan card's 'Cannot read the web on this computer' chip cannot be walked on the bench: the stand-in intake never plans a researcher task. A FORERUNNER_BENCH_PLAN option that adds a research task would let the helper's live check and future reviews see it end to end.

No screen sets a project's site list or block list. PUT /projects/:id/settings needs the version, which a client learns only from the 409 conflict answer; my walk hit the 409 first. The fixer reported this.

With the stand-in critic, a research task whose only page was refused ends Done and 'accepted'. That is the stand-in, which accepts everything. The helper's live check should confirm that the real critic, which is shown 'web page not read: ... (Refused ...)', sends such work back or says so.
